speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy with feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if you have been vomiting, and if so, is the vomit green or yellow?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is fussy and crying when the abdomen is touched, suggesting tenderness or severe discomfort. Can you tell me if the baby has passed any stool, and if so, does it look like "currant jelly" (red and black) or contain blood?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: No fever, vomiting, or diarrhea has been observed, and the baby was born at term without complications. Can you tell me if the baby has passed any stool, and if so, does it resemble "currant jelly" (dark red and black)?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception.

The clinical presentation of an 8-month-old with abdominal distension, feeding difficulties, irritability, and a history of decreased stool passage is highly suggestive of intussusception.
